Foo Fighters concert on Tuesday 10 November and Robbie Williams concert on Saturday 14 November at Accor Stadium.

With large crowds expected to attend both concerts at Accor Stadium, delays are expected on roads approaching the precinct. On Tuesday traffic is expected to be heavy during the already busy weeknight evening peak. On Saturday night traffic is expected to be heavy with a concert also on at the neighbouring Afterpay Arena.

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

  • PARKING: Car parks are expected to be in high demand, fans are urged to pre-book parking online ahead of time to secure a space. A flat rate $40 parking fee applies. 
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry. If you haven't pre-booked parking don't drive to Olympic Park.
  • Carpool with your group and allow plenty of extra travel time as traffic will be heavy on both nights.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter car park and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park, at no extra cost.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority will close local roads in the precinct and traffic congestion is expected before and after the match. For road closure details, visit the Sydney Olympic Park Authority interactive map.

properties.otherAdvice:
Up to 10,000 cyclists will ride from Sydney to Fairy Meadow for the annual MS Gong Ride. The 80km ride from Tempe Recreation Reserve starts from 6am and the 53km ride will start at Preston Park, Engadine from 8am. Both events finish at Thomas Dalton Park, Fairy Meadow by 3:30pm.

Road and lane closures will be in place along sections of the course.

  • 4am to 9:30am from Tempe to Sutherland: sections of West Botany St, Holbeach Ave and Bestic St. The speed limit will be reduced to 60/km along Rocky Point Rd/Taren Point Rd from Sans Souci to Taren Point.
  • 5am to 10am from Sutherland to Waterfall: Lane closures on the Princes Hwy from Kirrawee to Loftus and the speed limit will be reduced to 60km/h from Kirrawee to Waterfall. Delays are expected travelling southbound on the Princes Hwy during this time. 
  • 4am to 2:30pm in the Royal National Park: McKell Ave, Lady Wakehurst Dr, Sir Bertram Stevens Dr and Otford Rd. Access to the Royal National Park is via Farnell Ave only. The speed limit will be reduced to 40km/h along Lawrence Hargrave Dr from Stanwell Park to Thirroul from 6am to 3pm.
  • 5am to 4.30pm Stanwell Park to Fairy Meadow: sections of Elliotts Rd near the finish area will be closed and the speed limit reduced to 40km/h on sections of Elliotts Rd.

Motorists should exercise caution as cyclists will be sharing some roads along the course. Motorists are reminded when overtaking cyclists to leave a 1.5m distance on roads with speed limits over 60km/h and a 1m distance on roads 60km/h or under.

Special event clearways will be in place along key sections of the course between 4am and 3pm.

  • Tempe to Kirrawee (from 4am to 10am)
  • Princes Hwy (from 4am to 11am)
  • Stanwell Park to Fairy Meadow (from 5am to 3pm)

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed it will be relocated to the nearest legal parking space, use the Find My Car website or call 132 701 to find its new location
